title: Honorifics
body1: $C[960000]Honorifics$C[000000]$dJapanese uses honorifics to address people in everyday Japanese communication. Using specific honorifics depends on the relationship of the speaker and the person they are referring to, in addition to factors such as gender and hierarchy. The most common is -san, a gender neutral and polite honorific. Other common ones in anime and games are -chan for addressing a younger female or children, -kun for addressing younger males, and -senpai for addressing a superior. The honorific -sensei is used to address teachers as well as professions such as doctors.

body1: $C[960000]Kachikachi Yama$C[000000]$dKachikachi Yama is a Japanese folktale about a man who caught a raccoon dog and tied it to a tree to kill and cook later. When the man left for town, the raccoon dog cried and begged the man's wife who was making some mochi, a sweet rice dish, to set him free, promising he would help her.
